targets.name: Use the correct verb form after another verb or preposition
targets.reason: Verb-form errors remain the strongest recurring pattern. W32 added nine verb-form errors, and the three-week window contains 53 verb-form errors across 14 lesson days.
targets.trigger: Building a verb after need, should, stop, or to: use the correct complement and base or gerund form.

error_examples.correction: I need to ask for help.

error_examples.mistake: You need to stop your work and had a rest.
error_examples.correction: You should stop working and have a rest.

error_examples.mistake: He is to study hard to get a high score.
error_examples.correction: He needs to study hard to get a high score.

targets.name: Keep completed events in the past tense
targets.reason: W32 added ten tense errors in short accounts of dinner, work, and past experiences. The window contains 32 tense errors across 14 lesson days.
targets.trigger: Describing something that already happened: keep the main verbs consistently in the past tense.

error_examples.mistake: When I try to fix some problems, I find the time went flying.
error_examples.correction: When I try to fix something, I find that time flies so fast.

targets.name: Mark count nouns and choose the right determiner
targets.reason: W32 added eight plural, quantifier, and determiner errors involving permission, places, work, and responsibility. The window contains 44 related errors across 14 lesson days.
targets.trigger: Choosing a, the, no article, a plural form, or much/many/a lot of before a noun.

error_examples.mistake: You need to ask your boss to get a permission.
error_examples.correction: You need to ask your boss to get permission.

error_examples.mistake: My family members often take a trip, but to different cities or place.
error_examples.correction: My family members often take trips to different cities or places.
I have a lot of work.
